title: Assessment of toxic elements in sediments of Linggi River using NAA and ICP-MS techniques
author: Elias, Ibrahim, et al.
materials: σanalysed= standard deviation of analysed value
σcertified= standard deviation of certified value

steps.title: Prepare mixed standard solution
steps.instruction: Combine single‑element standards to make a mixed solution with defined concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Obtain single‑element standard solutions of As, Sb, Cr, Zn and Fe from Merck.
In a 100 mL volumetric flask, prepare a mixed standard solution containing As 10 mg/L, Sb 10 mg/L, Cr 80 mg/L, Zn 100 mg/L and Fe 1000 mg/L.

steps.title: Load standard onto filter paper
steps.instruction: Place a measured aliquot of the mixed standard on filter paper, dry, and seal the vial.

substeps.instruction: Insert a 1 cm diameter Whatman filter paper into a small polyethylene vial (Ø 1 cm × 3 cm height).
Pipette 0.2 mL (≈0.2 g) of the mixed standard solution onto the filter paper.
Dry the vial in an oven at 50 °C for 24 h.
Seal the vial with heating solder.

steps.title: Prepare sediment samples for irradiation
steps.instruction: Dry, grind, sieve, weigh, and seal sediment samples and SRM before irradiation.

substeps.instruction: Dry wet sediment samples in an oven at 60 °C until constant weight.
Grind the dried sediment to a fine powder using an agate mortar.
Sieve the powder through a 63 μm mesh sieve.
Weigh 0.15–0.20 g of homogenised sediment (or IAEA‑Soil‑7 SRM) into polyethylene vials.
Seal each vial with heating solder.

steps.title: Prepare ICP‑MS calibration standards
steps.instruction: Dilute commercial standard to generate a four‑point calibration curve.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the commercial mix standard solution (Standard® X) from Perkin Elmer.
Prepare calibration standards at 10 μg/L, 50 μg/L, 100 μg/L and 150 μg/L.

steps.title: Configure ICP‑MS instrument
steps.instruction: Set all operating parameters to the values specified for the analysis.

substeps.instruction: Set standby vacuum pressure to 2.8 × 10⁻⁶ Torr and plasma vacuum pressure to 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ Torr.
Set nebulizer gas flow to 0.98 L/min.
Set lens voltage to 6.3 V.
Set RF power to 1075.0 W.
Set analog stage voltage to –2150.0 V and pulse stage voltage to 1100.0 V.
Verify mass‑detection correlation coefficients: 111Cd R² = 0.999929, 63Cu R² = 0.999875, 60Ni R² = 0.999920, 208Pb R² = 0.999827 (all >0.9998).

steps.title: Analyze samples by ICP‑MS
steps.instruction: Run the sediment digests together with blanks and calibration standards on the ICP‑MS.

substeps.instruction: Digest each sediment sample (digestion details as used in the study) using reagent‑blank acid.
Introduce the digested sample into the Perkin Elmer‑Elan 6000 ICP‑MS and measure Pb, Cd, Cu and Ni concentrations.
Run the reagent‑blank acid periodically and use its signal to correct analytical results.
Generate a calibration curve from the four standards; confirm linearity with R² > 0.9998.

steps.title: Perform quality control with SRM
steps.instruction: Analyze the IAEA‑Soil‑7 reference material in the same way as samples and calculate QC metrics.

substeps.instruction: Analyze SRM IAEA‑Soil‑7 using the same ICP‑MS procedure.
Record certified and measured values for each element (Table 3):
• As (NAA): certified 13.4 ± 0.8 mg kg⁻¹, analysed 14.5 ± 1.0 mg kg⁻¹, recovery 108.2 %, relative bias 8.2 %, U‑test 0.86, CV 0.05 %, LOD 0.05 μg g⁻¹.
• Cr (NAA): certified 60 ± 14 μg g⁻¹, analysed 57.9 ± 5.0 μg g⁻¹, recovery 96.5 %, relative bias –2.5 %, U‑test 0.14, CV 0.61 %, LOD 0.05 μg g⁻¹.
• Fe (NAA): certified 25700 ± 600 mg kg⁻¹, analysed 25950 ± 1100 mg kg⁻¹, recovery 101.0 %, relative bias 1.0 %, U‑test 0.20, CV 0.40 %, LOD 0.01 %.
• Sb (NAA): certified 1.7 ± 0.3 mg kg⁻¹, analysed 1.81 ± 0.4 mg kg⁻¹, recovery 106.7 %, relative bias 6.7 %, U‑test 0.22, CV 2.2 %, LOD 0.05 μg g⁻¹.
• Zn (NAA): certified 104 ± 9 mg kg⁻¹, analysed 118 ± 21 mg kg⁻¹, recovery 113.4 %, relative bias 13.4 %, U‑test 1.52, CV 1.7 %, LOD 0.10 μg g⁻¹.
• Cd (ICP‑MS): certified 1.3 ± 0.2 μg L⁻¹, analysed 1.40 ± 0.1 μg L⁻¹, recovery 107.7 %, relative bias 7.7 %, U‑test 0.45, CV 0.71 %, LOD 5.0 ng L⁻¹.
• Cu (ICP‑MS): certified 11.0 ± 2.0 μg L⁻¹, analysed 12.4 ± 0.5 μg L⁻¹, recovery 112.7 %, relative bias 12.7 %, U‑test 0.68, CV 0.50 %, LOD 0.0 ng L⁻¹.
• Pb (ICP‑MS): certified 60.0 ± 11.0 μg L⁻¹, analysed 50.0 ± 5.0 μg L⁻¹, recovery 83.3 %, relative bias –16.7 %, U‑test 0.83, CV 1.0 %, LOD 0.02 ng L⁻¹.
• Ni (ICP‑MS): certified 26.0 ± 5.0 μg L⁻¹, analysed 21.2 ± 1.0 μg L⁻¹, recovery 81.5 %, relative bias –18.5 %, U‑test 0.94, CV 0.72 %, LOD 0.0 ng L⁻¹.
Calculate recovery = (C_analyzed / C_certified) × 100 % and confirm it lies between 81.5 % and 113.4 %.
Calculate coefficient of variation (CV) and confirm it lies between 4.0 % and 22.1 %.
Compute relative bias using Eq. (2): (C_analyzed – C_certified)/C_certified × 100 %.
Compute U‑test using Eq. (3): |C_analyzed – C_certified| / √(σ_analyzed² + σ_certified²).
Accept the result if U‑test ≤ 1.95.

steps.title: Interpret U‑test results
steps.instruction: Compare calculated U‑test scores to the decision thresholds.

substeps.instruction: U‑test ≤ 1.64 → result does not differ significantly from certified value.
1.64 < U‑test ≤ 1.95 → result probably does not differ significantly.
1.95 < U‑test ≤ 2.58 → significance unclear.
2.58 < U‑test ≤ 3.29 → result probably significantly different.
U‑test > 3.29 → result significantly different.
